chunks: The earth will light up with the effulgence of her Lord; and the ledger (of account) will be placed (in each man's hand), and the apostles and the witnesses will be called, and judgement passed between them equitably, and no wrong will be done to them.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the earth and the prophets on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia eschatological discourses, highlights the manifestation of Divine Light (Nur) as the ultimate reality of judgment, where the earth is illuminated by God's presence rather than the sun. It underscores the culmination of prophetic mission and the testimony of martyrs (Shuhada), affirming that divine justice is absolute and impartial, a theme central to the concept of Adl in Shia theology. The presentation of the 'Book' signifies the detailed accounting of deeds, ensuring no soul is wronged in its final reckoning.
